claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT can be used to identify and predict ferromagnetic ground states in complex alloys.
Spin-polarized DFT directly captures exchange interactions.
Energy differences between spin-aligned and non-spin-aligned configurations can establish the magnetic ground state.
The proposed material is a chemically disordered, high-temperature or quenched multicomponent alloy such as Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
The method compares total energies from spin-polarized and non-spin-polarized DFT calculations.
The proposed calculations represent the 0 K ground state under ideal periodic boundary conditions and without an external field.
Local chemical environments and short-range ordering of Co, Fe, and Ni affect local exchange interactions.
Spin-polarized DFT explicitly incorporates electron spin.
Spin-polarized DFT can calculate a lowering of total energy caused by parallel spin alignment.
A significant energy lowering of the magnetic solution indicates stabilization of a ferromagnetic ground state.
The spin-polarized state is predicted to have lower total energy than the non-spin-polarized state.
The predicted spin-polarized state has a nonzero net magnetic moment per formula unit.
A lower-energy spin-polarized state with a nonzero net moment indicates a ferromagnetic ground state.
A calculation without spin polarization yields a nonmagnetic baseline.
The method is expected to be reliable for alloys with substantial d-electron contributions, including alloys containing Co, Fe, or Ni.
Strong electron-correlation or disorder effects may make spin-polarized DFT less definitive and require beyond-DFT methods.
The calculated energy difference and magnetic moment may depend on the exchange-correlation functional, simulation-cell size, and treatment of disorder.
The proposed 0 K DFT treatment does not capture finite-temperature effects that may affect experimental ferromagnetism.
